plain.li: [opt2] Sent a parcel home, the coin sewn in where no thief would look. I hope it gets there before winter.
[opt3] I read {X_nameDef}'s letter out at supper. Now the others ask after people they've never met, and I love them for it.
[winter] A letter from {X_nameDef}, with frost on the wrapping. I read it close to the fire to make it last.
[opt0] Wrote back to {X_nameDef} by lamplight. It took me three tries to stop it sounding like a report.

warm.li: [opt2] Whatever I sent home, it isn't enough. But it's something with my hands on it.
[opt3] They laughed at {X_nameDef}'s jokes. Out loud, at the table. I'll write and tell {X_objective}.

cheerful.li: [opt3] They all want to know how the goats back home are doing now. I've made a colony of goat enthusiasts!

gloomy.li: [opt2] A parcel for home. It felt like sending a piece of myself somewhere I can't follow.

blunt.li: [opt2] Parcel's gone. Family will eat well for once.

cold.li: [opt3] Read the letter out. They wanted to hear it.

plain.li: [winter] Went down on the ice today and got up again. The cards said bad luck. I say that was it.
[trait:Nervous] I've been jumping at every noise since the fortune teller came. Today something nearly happened, and didn't. I can breathe again.
Missed by a hand's width. If that was the bad fortune, it was a poor one.

warm.li: The others made me sit down with something hot after my fright, and wouldn't let me up until I'd drunk all of it.

cheerful.li: Bad fortune: used up. I'm walking under every ladder in the colony tomorrow.

cold.li: Near miss. The cards were wrong, or right. It doesn't matter now.

plain.li: [opt2] {X_nameDef} went home with gifts for the family that searched for {X_objective} all those years ago. I hope they remember us at their table.
[opt3] {X_nameDef} spent the day at our workbench and went home with a trade. The lost child, learning a craft. I keep shaking my head over it.
[opt0] There's a bed in the colony with {X_nameDef} in it. I've looked in twice, as if {X_pronoun} might wander off again.

cheerful.li: [opt0] {X_nameDef} is staying! I found {X_objective} once, and now {X_pronoun} found us.

gloomy.li: [opt1] {X_nameDef} came and went in a day. They grow up and they leave, even the ones who were never ours.

cold.li: [opt2] Gave the family some silver. {X_nameDef} seemed grateful.

plain.li: [opt3] We told the market {X_nameDef} drowned in the river. {X_nameDef} is sleeping in the spare bed tonight, very much alive.

cheerful.li: [opt3] The best story I ever told was the one about {X_nameDef} drowning. Even I nearly believed it.

gloomy.li: [opt3] A lie to save a life. I'd tell it again, but I don't like how easily it came.
